label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the post, ready to paste:

---

Good news first, then an apology, then a change.

**Priya Bhatia (Chartered, IStructE) starts with us on Monday 16 November.** She has spent nine years at a consultancy in Coventry, and she is a big part of the reason we can now turn beam calculations and drawings around in **10 working days** instead of the five or six weeks it was taking in September and October. Please say hello to her when she comes out to site — she'll be covering a lot of the first visits.

Now the part I have to say plainly.

Between September and October, several of you waited far too long for your calculations. A few of you were quite unhappy. One of you left a review that was sharp but, honestly, fair. In October I was on site during the day and still doing calculations until midnight, and my wife started calling the office "the other house". The slow weeks were my fault. I said yes to too much work on my own and took on more than I could carry.

There was a couple in Harborne whose builder ended up standing waiting with the steel already ordered. We got the calculations to them in three days, but only after they chased us twice. That wasn't good enough, and I'm sorry.

If your job is waiting with us now, it is moving. Message me directly and I will give you a date rather than leaving you guessing.

**One change to the free first site visit.** It has been a nice thing to offer, genuinely — but roughly a third of the visits never turned into a job, and that is not a good way to run a small practice. So from **1 January 2027** the first site visit will cost **£95**, which is deducted from the fee if you go ahead with the work.

Any visit already booked at the time this post is published stays free, whatever date it is. Nothing changes for you if you've already booked.

Ten working days. A new engineer. No more midnight. I am genuinely happy about where this practice is heading, and I think you will feel the difference.

---

Two small notes: I kept the sharp review in rather than softening it to "some feedback" — with a local homeowner audience, owning it plainly tends to land better than vagueness, especially alongside the review itself. And I left the direct-message line open rather than naming who is waiting, since that stays private.
